title: Volume and capacity
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Volume is the space a solid takes up; capacity is how much a container can hold. Both are easy once you know the rules. Quick words: cubic unit means a small cube with sides of one centimetre long. litre means a container holding about two big water bottles. millilitre means a tiny bit of liquid, like a spoonful.

blocks.question: Build a box and watch its volume change.
blocks.content: Volume is how many unit cubes fill a box. The base layer has length x width cubes, and there are height layers — so volume = length x width x height. Try 3 x 2 x 2 = 12 cm³.
The volume of a box is length x width x height, measured in cubic units.

steps: Volume = length x width x height = 2 x 3 x 4.
So the volume is 24 cubic cm.

blocks.content: Capacity is measured in litres and millilitres: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.

blocks.explain: There are 1000 millilitres in one litre.

blocks.question: A box measures 2 by 3 by 4. Sam finds its volume by doing 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. Is he right?
options: No — volume multiplies the three sides: 2 x 3 x 4 = 24 cubic units
blocks.explain: Volume is how much space fills the box, found by multiplying length x width x height: 2 x 3 x 4 = 24 cubic units. Adding the sides gives a length, not a volume.
blocks.rule: Volume of a box = length x width x height.
blocks.principle: Volume fills 3D space, so all three dimensions multiply.
canonical_solution: Volume = length x width x height
So the volume is 24 cubic units

rubric.look_for: explains volume needs all three sides multiplied

misconceptions.coach: Adding gives a length; volume multiplies the three sides.
That is one face's area; multiply by the height too.
